newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Uralsvyazinform raises Q1 97 dividend.
newsitem.headline: Russian Uralsvyazinform raises Q1 97 dividend.

text.p: Russian telecom Uralsvyazinform raised its first quarter dividend to 0.11 roubles, which is more than double the equivalent dividend from that period in 1996, a securities department official said on Monday.

Dmitry Kondakov said the dividend in the first quarter of 1996, which the board of directors sets, was 600 roubles and the stock was subsequently split twice for a total of 13,164 times. Thus the first quarter 1996 dividend in 1997 terms would be 0.05 roubles.
The Urals mountains-based telecom does not have preferred shares.

It said 1996 dividends, which have been paid out, were 0.5916 roubles after 4.3200 roubles in 1995, before a 12:1 split. That would be 0.5916 roubles for 1996 compared to 0.3600 roubles for 1995 in 1996 terms.

These figures are not prepared to international accounting standards but to Russian accounting standards, which differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
